topics.label: Course introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This topic provides the introductory framing and pedagogical overview for the cancer biology lecture series.

topics.label: Cancer as a disruption of cellular differentiation and tissue architecture
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics define cancer as a breakdown of genetic programs, cellular differentiation, and three-dimensional tissue architecture, while addressing the limitations of studying this biology in two-dimensional cell culture.

topics.label: Distinguishing benign and malignant tumors by invasion, progression, and nomenclature
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the clinical, histological, and terminological distinctions between benign and malignant neoplasms, focusing on basement membrane invasion and metastatic potential.

topics.label: Mechanisms of cancer morbidity and mortality
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic addresses the specific physiological and systemic mechanisms through which primary and metastatic tumors cause disease and death.

topics.label: Tumor incidence in humans and across multicellular organisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the frequency of different tumor types in human populations and across animal species, framing cancer as a universal consequence of multicellular development.

topics.label: Cancer screening principles and clinical diagnostic methods
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the clinical rationale, histological indicators, and practical challenges of population screening programs for early cancer detection.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and practical reminders
topics.groupedBecause: This topic provides the closing framing, concluding the lecture and directing students toward their upcoming practicals.
